title: ध्वन्यात्मक अभिव्यञ्जनाका दृष्टिमा पागल कविता {Crazy poetry in terms of phonetic expressions}
nepali: महाकवि लक्ष्मीप्रसाद देवकोटाद्वारा रचित ‘पागल’ कवितामा के कस्तो ध्वन्यात्मक अभिव्यञ्जना पाइन्छ तथा उक्त कवितामा अत्यन्ततिरस्कृत वाच्यध्वनि कसरी प्रयुक्त भएको छ भन्ने प्राज्ञिक समस्याको समाधानमा केन्द्रित ‘ध्वन्यात्मक अभिव्यञ्जनाका दृष्टिमा पागल कविता’ शीर्षकको प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखका निम्ति आवश्यक सामग्रीको सङ्कलन पुस्तकालयीय विधिका आधारमा गरिएको छ भने सामग्रीको विश्लेषण निमनात्मक पद्धतिका आधारमा गरिएको छ । ध्वनिसम्बन्धी सैद्धान्तिक आधार निर्माणका निम्ति क्रमशः आनन्दवर्धनको ध्वन्यालोक, अभिनव गुप्तको ध्वन्यालोकलोचन (ध्वन्यालोकको टीका), मम्मटको काव्यप्रकाश, विश्वनाथको साहित्यदर्पण र जगन्नाथको रसगङ्गाधर नामक ग्रन्थका ध्वनिसिद्धान्तसम्बन्धी स्थापनाहरूको अनुशीलन गरिएको छ र त्यही सैद्धान्तिक आधारमा‘पागल’ कविताको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । ‘पागल’ कवितामा देवकोटाको मानवतावादी चेतनाका साथै व्यङ्ग्य–विद्रोहको चेतना कलात्मक रूपमा अभिव्यक्त भएको कुरा औँल्याइएको छ । यस कवितामा प्रयुक्त पदावलीमा कोमल तथा परुष दुवै किसिमका शब्दको चयन तथा समानान्तर संयोजन, सामान्यता तथा गहनताको द्वैधता एवं मानक र विचलनको खिंचातानी हास्यव्यङ्ग्यचेतका निम्ति सशक्त साधन बन्न पुगेको छ । कवितामा कतै सौन्दर्यप्रेम त कतै क्रान्ति चेतना, कतै मानवीय करुणामयता त कतै हास्यास्पद समसामयिक राजनैतिक नाटकीयताप्रति तीव्र व्यङ्ग्य प्रहार गरिएको पाइन्छ । यस सन्दर्भमा कहीं कुसुम झैं कोमल त कहीं वज्रझैं कठोर बिम्बप्रतीक तथा अलङ्कारहरूको समानान्तर वितरण तथा आयोजनाले पनि हास्यगर्भित व्यङ्ग्य– विद्रोहचेतनाको संयोजनमा प्रभावकारी भूमिका खेलेको र कतिपय ठाउँमा उपमानका रूपमा आएका पाश्चात्य एवं पूर्वीय मिथकीय सन्दर्भले पनि कलात्मक सौन्दर्यको सिर्जना गरेको निष्कर्ष दिइएको छ ।
american_english: This research article, titled "The Poem 'Pagal' from the Perspective of Phonetic Expression," is centered on resolving the academic problem of what kind of phonetic expression is found in the poem "Pagal" composed by Mahakavi Laxmi Prasad Devkota and how the highly denigrated audible voice is used in that poem. For this article, the necessary materials were collected on the basis of the library method, while the analysis of the materials was carried out on the basis of a deductive method. To construct a theoretical foundation related to sound, the sound-related propositions in the texts Dhvanyaloka by Anandavardhana, Dhvanyalokalocana (a commentary on Dhvanyaloka) by Abhinavagupta, Kavyaprakasha by Mammata, Sahityadarpana by Vishvanatha, and Rasagangadhara by Jagannatha were studied sequentially, and the poem "Pagal" was analyzed on that same theoretical basis. It is pointed out that in the poem "Pagal," along with Devkota's humanistic consciousness, a consciousness of satire and rebellion has been artistically expressed. In the vocabulary used in this poem, the selection and parallel combination of both soft and harsh kinds of words, the duality of generality and profundity, and the tension between standard and deviation have become powerful devices for the consciousness of humor and satire. In the poem, a love of beauty is found in some places and revolutionary consciousness in others, human compassion in some places and a sharp satirical attack on the ridiculous contemporary political theatricality in others. In this context, it has been concluded that the parallel distribution and arrangement of imagery, symbols, and figures of speech—at times as soft as a flower and at times as hard as a thunderbolt—have also played an effective role in combining a humor-laden consciousness of satire and rebellion, and that in certain places the Western and Eastern mythological references appearing as similes have also created artistic beauty.

informal_english: This research article, titled "The Poem 'Pagal' from the Perspective of Phonetic Expression," is all about sorting out the academic question of what sort of phonetic expression turns up in the poem "Pagal" by Mahakavi Laxmi Prasad Devkota and how the much-scorned audible voice is put to use in that poem. For this piece, the needed material was gathered using the library method, while the analysis of that material was done on the basis of a deductive method. To build a theoretical footing for sound, the sound-related ideas in the texts Dhvanyaloka by Anandavardhana, Dhvanyalokalocana (a commentary on Dhvanyaloka) by Abhinavagupta, Kavyaprakasha by Mammata, Sahityadarpana by Vishvanatha, and Rasagangadhara by Jagannatha were gone through in turn, and the poem "Pagal" was analysed on that same theoretical ground. It's pointed out that in the poem "Pagal," alongside Devkota's humanistic awareness, a sense of satire and rebellion has been put across in an artistic way. In the words used in this poem, the picking and parallel pairing of both soft and harsh kinds of words, the mix of the everyday and the profound, and the tug-of-war between the standard and the deviant have become strong tools for a consciousness of humour and satire. In the poem, you find a love of beauty in some places and revolutionary awareness in others, human compassion in some places and a sharp satirical jab at the ridiculous contemporary political carry-on in others. In that light, it's concluded that the parallel spread and arrangement of imagery, symbols, and figures of speech—at times as soft as a flower and at times as hard as a thunderbolt—have also played a cracking role in bringing together a humour-laced sense of satire and rebellion, and that in some spots the Western and Eastern mythological references turning up as similes have also created artistic beauty.
translator_notes: The title term 'पागल' is retained as "Pagal" in translations to preserve the poem's established name. The phrase 'अत्यन्ततिरस्कृत वाच्यध्वनि' is rendered as 'highly denigrated audible voice/scorned audible voice' in line with the paper's phonetic/dhvani focus; sentence order has been kept strictly parallel to the Nepali.
